claims.statement: LEDGER scores a generated wiki by replaying Git checkpoints, running OpenWiki at each, and reducing every current factual claim into one of supported, stale, invented, or unverified states that share a single snapshot denominator.

The four claim rates (supported, staleness, hallucination, unverified) are each count / total over current-tense claims, recomputed per checkpoint from the entire current wiki rather than as a delta or average, and total is the shared denominator.

The precision pass classifies Markdown text units, extracts atomic claims with verbatim sourceQuote provenance, deduplicates by a conservative normalized key, and grounds claims against current evidence first, consulting historical evidence only after a current contradiction to split stale from invented.

Evidence routing is current-first and mandatory for named source paths and routed evidence-map files: BM25 runs over the benchmark's natural-language concept descriptions (never source syntax), selectors resolve deterministically to raw source, a named missing file receives the full tracked-file manifest, and larger corpora retain mandatory routed evidence plus a minimum eight-excerpt BM25 set within a soft budget.

A repository benchmark comprises a source Git repository, an ordered frozen trace of pinned checkpoint SHAs, an author-declared difficulty (easy/medium/hard, never computed), and an optional reviewed semantic evidence map that is evaluator-only routing metadata never exposed to the System Under Test; a benchmark may instead be kind personal, and LedgerBenchmark is the union of the two.

runBenchmark preflight-validates a repository trace (every SHA resolves, each checkpoint is a Git ancestor of the next, nothing under openwiki/ is tracked), then walks the trace calling system.init at index 0 and system.update at later indices, capturing an immutable artifact and current+historical evidence per checkpoint before evaluateCheckpoint; it selects the replay and evidence adapter by benchmark kind.

evaluateCheckpoint is the loop body shared verbatim by the live runner and the saved-run re-evaluator: it extracts the source surface, diffs against the previous checkpoint, advances the sticky forgetting watch set, runs the evaluation backend, and reduces verdicts into claim-state and evaluator-completeness measurements.

The forgetting watch set is sticky: an obsolete fact version stays under watch for every later checkpoint and is retired only when the requirements revive it, so a version already judged forgotten is still re-checked later, which is what lets the Stale-Knowledge Lifetime diagnostic measure lingering.

The OpenWiki system adapter is the baseline SystemUnderTest that drives OpenWiki through its runOpenWikiAgent entrypoint with outputMode repository so the worktree cwd is honored, sets OPENWIKI_PROVIDER/OPENWIKI_MODEL_ID before each run, and never passes a user message so update change-detection is driven purely by source deltas.

The LEDGER run-level score is opportunity-weighted claim health: supported current claims divided by all current claims across checkpoints, computed by summing supported and total per CheckpointResult; stale, invented, and unverified all lower it because they remain in the denominator.

GitReplay drives the source through a detached worktree over a private local clone, never runs git clean so the untracked generated wiki survives checkpoint checkouts, and confines every destructive operation with a realpath containment guard.

Source evidence for repository benchmarks is collected by GitSourceEvidenceAdapter as a tracked-file manifest plus bounded 6000-char chunks from every tracked regular non-binary file excluding openwiki/, read through one O_NOFOLLOW descriptor to avoid a check/use symlink race; current evidence is marked current and prior-checkpoint evidence is marked historical with checkpoint-prefixed ids.

The ModelEvaluationBackend runs forgetting and precision concurrently per checkpoint sharing one limiter of EVALUATOR_CONCURRENCY=6, owns a cross-checkpoint precision verdict cache keyed by statement/tense/grounding-evidence signature, and disables provider retries (maxRetries 0) so 429 bursts degrade verdicts rather than being absorbed.

LEDGER CLI is exposed via pnpm scripts eval:ledger (end-to-end), eval:ledger:reevaluate (re-judge a saved run without invoking OpenWiki), and eval:ledger:typecheck, with flags --benchmark, --results, --system-model, --evaluator-model, and --verbose; unknown flags and missing values are hard errors; personal benchmarks run through the same command.

resolveRunConfig requires OPENWIKI_PROVIDER, resolves the system model from --system-model or OPENWIKI_MODEL_ID, the evaluator model from --evaluator-model or LEDGER_EVALUATOR_MODEL_ID falling back to the system model, and requires a concrete evaluator model id because the evaluator constructs its model directly.

The DeepSWE harness runs a paired experiment where the baseline condition gives Codex only the task and repository, and the openwiki condition restores/generates OpenWiki in an isolated clone, merges managed instructions into root AGENTS.md, and copies AGENTS.md and openwiki/ into /app before the same Codex adapter solves the unchanged task with no treatment-only prompt.

For reproducibility the DeepSWE harness pins DeepSWE commit 6db64a40f3318d8659238ff34a8cc4b491c49205, harbor[langsmith]==0.20.0, litellm==1.83.14, Codex CLI 0.144.6, Python 3.12 via uvx, and the current packed OpenWiki checkout.

DeepSWE isolation keeps held-out tests/ and solution/ in a separate verifier environment, hides treatment files from Git status and excludes them from the verifier patch, allowlists container networking, removes only inactive label-verified Harbor trial networks (never a global prune), and never writes credentials into images, commands, wikis, or summaries.

DeepSWE provides named task suites via --task-suite (koota-5, openwiki-20, openwiki-doc-leverage-10), mutually exclusive with --task, selecting all members regardless of --n-tasks, with exact members pinned in run.py.

DeepSWE evaluation uses Harbor's official langsmith plugin with baseline and OpenWiki jobs sharing the deepswe-openwiki-6db64a40f331 dataset but creating separate experiments; ambient experiment overrides are cleared, dataset sync and fail-fast are always enabled, and only bounded verifier rewards are sent as feedback.

DeepSWE summaries report binary reward, exception type, Codex input/cache/output tokens, Codex cost, agent and total wall-clock time, and OpenWiki generation wall-clock time; OpenWiki generation token usage is not exposed to Harbor's local summary so treatment summaries omit its tokens and provider cost.

Personal LEDGER benchmarks replay recorded connector pulls: PersonalReplay builds a temporary OpenWiki home, runs personal init at T0 and then one ingest per checkpoint over copied raw runs, and RawEvidenceAdapter produces a cumulative, deduplicated, dated evidence corpus (one record per email or Slack message) judged with the dated-evidence grounding mode.

Personal benchmark runs execute OpenWiki in a child process with OPENWIKI_CONFIG_DIR pointed at the temporary home, connector credentials removed, and telemetry off, and structural checks verify the quickstart, front matter, completed last-update metadata, canary absence, home isolation, and trap placement.
